deities: Shiva (Jyotirlinga in front of the deity)

history.period: Traditional claim ~1200 years old; association with Adi Shankaracharya (8th century CE)
history.summary: The temple enshrines Goddess Mookambika, who (per legend) destroyed the demon Mookasura. Tradition holds that Adi Shankaracharya meditated on Kodachadri peak (~21 km away) and had a vision of the goddess here; he installed the Srichakra and the Shankara Simhasanam stone marks his penance spot. The seated goddess idol bears sankha and chakra in her upper hands with abhaya and varada mudras below, and a Jyotirlinga with a golden line stands before it. Shrines to Veerabhadra, Subramanya, Naga, Vinayaka and Anjaneya sit in the complex. One of Karnataka's seven Mukti Sthalas.

name: Sri Mookambika Temple
town_description: Kollur is a village in Kundapura taluk of Udupi district, Karnataka, nestled in the Western Ghats on the banks of the Sauparnika river. It is famous across South India as the home of the Sri Mookambika Temple, one of Karnataka's seven Mukti Sthalas, drawing lakhs of pilgrims for Navaratri and the Phalguna chariot festival. Nearby Kodachadri peak, where Adi Shankaracharya is said to have meditated, adds to its religious and trekking significance.

travel.railway: Byndoor/Mookambika Road station ~20 km (verify); Kundapura ~40 km (verify)
travel.road: Kollur is well connected by road and daily bus services from Mangalore, Shimoga, Sagara and Bangalore

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navaratri (September-October) is the biggest festival
